_source: AI-researched venue CANDIDATES for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly edited by the research agent. Populated by a daily scheduled research agent (2026-08, at explicit user request: 'fan out some research agents who's goal is to run every day to find and suggest new businesses... they shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet'; bumped from ~3-5/day to 10/day at a later explicit request). See .claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md for the full research brief/rules this agent works under (Hard rule 1 chain/fast-food screening, real coordinates only, no duplicates, Do/Drink/Eat coverage balance). The research agent commits straight to master for this file (no PR — this queue has zero effect on the live app, nothing reads it except the review agent and the admin dashboard's Growth Insights context). A second, independent daily agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) re-verifies each `pending` entry and is the only thing that ever promotes one into the real docs/data/venues.json, behind its own pull request — see that file's own doc comment for why the human checkpoint lives there instead of here. Each entry mirrors docs/data/venues.json's own raw shape (name/district/type/spend/lat/lon/base/bands/reason) exactly, so a reviewed-and-approved entry can be moved into that file with a straight copy-paste, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) that get stripped on promotion. `district` values must be a real existing district id from docs/data/districts.json (manchester/cheshire metros only) UNLESS the entry is itself proposing a brand-new district — see district-suggestions.json for that case instead; a venue suggestion should never invent a district id that doesn't exist anywhere.
_reviewWorkflow: status starts 'pending' on every new entry. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent changes it to 'approved' (then copies the venue fields into docs/data/venues.json and removes the entry here, as part of its own PR) or 'rejected' (left here with researchNotes explaining why, as a record so the same candidate isn't re-suggested later — curia-research-daily checks every entry here regardless of status before suggesting anything new). A human's actual review happens by reading/merging the review agent's PR, not by editing this file directly, though a human reviewer (or a future admin-dashboard screen) can still hand-edit an entry's status here if needed.

suggestions.name: Hallé St Peter's
suggestions.reason: A deconsecrated Grade II church on Blossom Street, still the Hallé's own rehearsal hall — public concerts land in a room built for hymn acoustics, not a sound engineer.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via halle.co.uk (official venue page) and Visit Manchester/Ticketline listings — Grade II listed former church at 40 Blossom Street, Ancoats M4 6BF, the Hallé Orchestra's own rehearsal/recording venue and a real public concert space (Oglesby Centre extension opened 2019). Single, unique site — not a chain (it's the Hallé's own building, not a franchised venue brand). Fills Ancoats' real Do-category gap (previously zero Do venues in the district despite 4 Eat/Drink venues there). Coordinates from a geocoded neighbouring Blossom Street address (39 Blossom St, same postcode M4 6BF) — street-level, not a district centroid. New type on this file, LIVE MUSIC, already exists (Band on the Wall). Confidence: high.

suggestions.name: BAB NQ
suggestions.reason: Flatbreads made from scratch in an open theatre kitchen, and a basement cocktail room that only unlocks once the sun's properly down.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via babnq.co.uk (official site), Creative Tourist and Visit Manchester listings — 14 Little Lever St, Manchester M1 1HR. Single-site independent (search turned up no second location); a genuinely fiercely-independent kebab/meze restaurant with a weekend-only basement cocktail bar, not a chain. Fills Northern Quarter's real Eat-category gap (the district had 4 Drink venues and zero Eat venues seeded). Coordinates geocoded from the M1 1HR postcode centroid (Little Lever Street itself). MIDDLE EASTERN type already exists (Heddy's, Wilmslow). Confidence: high.

suggestions.name: Smolensky Gallery
suggestions.reason: Polished concrete and street-art pedigree inside the ABC Building on Quay Street — worth a detour on the way to dinner, not an afterthought once you've eaten.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via smolenskygallery.com (official site), Manchester's Finest and Tripadvisor — ABC Building, 21-23 Quay Street, Manchester M3 4AE. Contemporary/urban art gallery, single Manchester site, no chain footprint found. Fills Spinningfields' real Do-category gap (the district had zero Do venues seeded — only Drink/Eat). Coordinates from Quay Street's own geocoded position. ART GALLERY type already exists (Manchester Art Gallery, Ricardo Van Parmar Gallery). Confidence: high.

suggestions.name: Podium Restaurant
suggestions.reason: Two AA Rosettes some forty floors below Cloud 23, and a kitchen more assured than the view it's sitting under.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via podiummanchester.com (official site), IHG's own hotel dining page and Confidentials review — 303 Deansgate, Manchester M3 4LQ, inside Beetham Tower (The Manchester Deansgate Hotel, formerly Hilton Manchester Deansgate). This is a single-site restaurant operated within a chain hotel building, the same precedent already accepted in this file for Refuge (Principal Hotel bar) and The Ivy Spinningfields — the restaurant brand itself (Podium) is not multi-site. Fills Deansgate's real Eat-category gap (the district had zero Eat venues seeded — only Drink/Do). Coordinates from Beetham Tower's own geocoded position. FINE DINING type already exists (The Ivy Spinningfields). Confidence: high.

suggestions.name: Hale Country Club & Spa
suggestions.reason: Five thermal rooms and an infinity pool looking out over its own acreage of Cheshire countryside — a members' club that still takes you for the day.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via halecountryclub.co.uk (official site), Good Spa Guide and ESPA's own location page — Clay Lane, Hale/Timperley, Cheshire WA15 7AF. Purpose-built single health club and spa; owned by THG (The Hut Group, an online retail/tech company, since 2016) but operates as one physical facility, not a multi-site club chain — no second Hale Country Club location found anywhere. Fills Hale's real Do-category gap (the district had zero Do venues seeded — only one Drink and one Eat). Coordinates from the WA15 7AF postcode centroid (Clay Lane). New type for the Do category catalogue map (SPA already exists, currently unused by any seeded venue) — maps to the 'Spa & wellness' onboarding tile. Confidence: medium-high (THG ownership noted for transparency, but it's a single site, same test already applied to other single-site venues under corporate ownership).

suggestions.name: The Yard
suggestions.reason: A greengrocer, a bakery and a juice bar built round a shared courtyard since 2012 — market-hall energy squeezed onto a converted Cheshire builder's plot.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via alderleyedge.com's own restaurant directory, Hungry Hoss and Sarah Thain's independent write-ups — 32 South Street, Alderley Edge SK9 7ES. Cooperative greengrocer/artisan butchery/organic bakery/juice bar opened 2012 by the Pickering family, with a café/events courtyard hosting markets, exhibitions and supper clubs — single independent site, no chain footprint. Fills Alderley Edge's real Do-category gap (the district had zero Do venues seeded — only Drink/Eat). Coordinates from the SK9 7ES postcode centroid (South Street). MARKET HALL type already exists (Mackie Mayor, Altrincham Market). Confidence: high.

suggestions.name: Barnshaw Smithy
suggestions.reason: Poached eggs and proper coffee next to a working reclamation yard, on the lane between Mobberley and Ashley that the sat-nav still hesitates over.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via barnshaw-smithy.com (official site), Tripadvisor 2026 reviews and food hygiene ratings register — Pepper Street, Mobberley, Knutsford WA16 6JH. A café combined with a reclamation/salvage yard, serving breakfast and lunch; single independent site sitting between Mobberley and Ashley villages, no chain footprint. Fills Mobberley's real Eat-category gap (the district had zero Eat venues seeded — only Drink/Do). Coordinates approximated from a neighbouring Pepper Street address (same short lane, WA16 6JL) since the exact WA16 6JH centroid wasn't independently geocodable — street-level, not a district centroid. BRUNCH SPOT type already exists (Caramello, Aldeli). Confidence: high on the venue being real/independent; medium on the exact coordinate (same street, adjacent postcode).

suggestions.name: Nam
suggestions.reason: Manchester's only true audiophile sound system, assembled by the team behind London's Brilliant Corners, running in the basement of a Vietnamese kitchen that keeps going long after the DJs start.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via nammcr.com (official site), Manchester's Finest, About Manchester and Creative Tourist — 33 Blossom Street, Ancoats M4 6AJ. Independent, family-run Vietnamese kitchen and basement 'listening space' bar, single site, no chain footprint found. Adds to Ancoats' thin Drink coverage (previously only The Jane Eyre) with a genuinely distinct format rather than a duplicate cocktail bar. Coordinates from a neighbouring Blossom Street geocode (same block as Hallé St Peter's, above). LISTENING BAR type already exists in src/lib/scoring/tile-catalog-map.ts's CATEGORY_BY_VENUE_TYPE (mapped to Drink) but had no venue using it yet — this is its first. Confidence: high.

suggestions.name: ATOMECA Wine Bar
suggestions.reason: Schofield's own second act on The Avenue — a walk-in wine list built around small plates, not the cocktail menu working next door.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via atomeca.co.uk (official site), Spinningfields' own directory and Square Meal/OpenTable listings — Unit G21, The Avenue, Spinningfields, Manchester M3 3HF. Run by the same team (James Brandwood, Joe and Daniel Schofield) as Schofield's Bar, already seeded in this app's Northern Quarter entry — this is the identical sibling-ownership precedent already established in venues.json for Craig's/Ivy Spinningfields (single second site from the same small team, not a multi-city chain). Fills Spinningfields' thin Drink coverage (previously only 20 Stories, itself more rooftop-restaurant than bar). Coordinates from the M3 3HF postcode centroid (The Avenue). WINE BAR type already exists (The Old Cellars, The Wine Cellar). Confidence: high.

suggestions.name: Riva Bar & Restaurant
suggestions.reason: Cecil Road's quieter answer to Hale's louder terraces — a proper wine list, unhurried service, and a Sunday lunch regulars book a week out for.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via rivahale.uk (official site), Tripadvisor and Square Meal listings — 4 Cecil Road, Hale, Altrincham WA15 9PA, a stone's throw from Hale railway station. Self-described 'fine dining' lounge bar and restaurant; single site, no chain footprint found (search for other Riva locations in the area returned none). Adds a second Eat option to Hale (previously only Victors). Coordinates anchored to Hale's own verified district centre (docs/data/districts.json) with a small real-world offset toward the village/station, since an independently-geocoded WA15 9PA result returned a longitude implausibly far from Hale's known position (likely a bad postcode-centroid match) — used the more reliable anchor rather than a suspect data point. WINE BAR/FINE DINING type already exists. Confidence: medium-high (address and independence well-verified; exact coordinate is a careful approximation rather than a clean geocode).
